landing.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
landing.faq.description: Answers about creating with Genjutsu AI: photos, effects, pricing and formats.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

landing.faq.shorts.answer: Yes. Choose a 9:16 effect or set the video size to 9:16, then download the MP4 ready to upload. Videos run up to 10 seconds.

landing.faq.ads.answer: Yes. Upload your own clip as the motion reference, add a photo of a presenter who has agreed to appear, and generate variations to test.
landing.faq.models.question: Which AI models are available?
landing.faq.models.answer: Character swaps run on Kling video-edit models, which keep the motion and camera of the reference clip and recast the lead from your photo.

landing.faq.commercial.question: Can I use the results commercially?

landing.about.p2: Create videos with Seedance 2.0 and Seedance 2.0 Fast using one credit balance. Draft a scene on a fast model, then render the take you like in cinematic 1080p without leaving the studio.
landing.about.p3: Every render is priced in credits, and you see the cost before you click Generate. If a generation fails, the credits come back automatically, so experimenting never feels like a gamble.

landing.how.title: From photo to post in three moves
landing.faq.what.question: What is Genjutsu AI?
landing.faq.what.answer: Genjutsu AI is a browser-based AI video tool. Upload one photo, pick an effect or your own video, and it swaps you into the scene while keeping the motion and camera. Videos download as MP4 files for social media, ads and websites.
landing.faq.prompt.question: Which photo works best?
landing.faq.prompt.answer: Use a sharp, well-lit photo of one person with the face clearly visible. Avoid group photos, heavy filters and sunglasses, and only upload people who have agreed to appear in your video.

landing.guide.p1: Higgsfield Genjutsu edits existing footage through motion transfer or targeted object swaps.
landing.guide.p2: This site is an independent tool and is not affiliated with Higgsfield; compare workflows before choosing.
landing.tutorial.title: How to make a Genjutsu AI video
landing.tutorial.description: A full walkthrough, from a blank prompt to a downloaded MP4. Most first clips take under five minutes.
landing.tutorial.open.title: Open the studio
landing.tutorial.open.description: Go to Create and choose Video. Sign in so your credits and render history stay with your account.
landing.tutorial.describe.title: Describe the shot
landing.tutorial.describe.description: Name the subject, what it does, where it happens and the light. Add one camera move, such as a slow dolly-in or a handheld follow.
landing.tutorial.format.title: Set the format
landing.tutorial.format.description: Pick Seedance 2.0 Fast for drafts or Seedance 2.0 for final takes, then 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1, 480p to 1080p, and 5 or 10 seconds. The credit cost updates as you choose.
landing.tutorial.render.title: Render and review
landing.tutorial.render.description: Press Generate. Clips usually arrive in one to three minutes and are saved to Recent creations, so you can leave the page while they render.
landing.tutorial.iterate.title: Iterate, then post
landing.tutorial.iterate.description: Change one detail per take, keep the version that works, and download the MP4 for TikTok, Reels, Shorts or an ad.
landing.tutorial.note: Following a Higgsfield Genjutsu tutorial instead? That workflow is different: upload a 3 to 30 second clip, add images of the character or product, choose Motion Transfer or Object Swap, then render. It edits existing footage, while the steps above create footage from scratch.
landing.effects.title: Change outfits, weather and scenes with a word
landing.effects.description: Every clip starts from text, so restyling a scene means editing a phrase, not masking frames. Keep the subject and camera line the same and swap one detail per take.
landing.compare.title: Genjutsu vs Seedance: which fits your shot?
landing.compare.description: Seedance creates new footage from a written description. Reference editing starts with a filmed take and offers a different kind of control.

landing.compare.input.seedance: A text prompt, no footage needed

landing.compare.control.seedance: Subject, setting, light, style and camera move

landing.compare.resolution.label: Resolution
landing.compare.cost.label: Typical cost
landing.compare.cost.genjutsu: About $2 (480p) to $7.20 (1080p) per 15 s clip, as reported at launch
landing.compare.best.label: Best for
landing.compare.best.genjutsu: Recasting footage, product and outfit swaps
landing.compare.best.seedance: New ideas, B-roll, ads and shorts with no filming

landing.free.title: Is Genjutsu AI free?
landing.free.p1: Registration, template browsing and opening examples are free.
landing.free.p2: Video generation uses prepaid balance. Packs start at $9.90 with no subscription; failed generations automatically return the deducted balance.

landing.faq.higgsfield.answer: No. Genjutsu AI is an independent AI video studio with no affiliation to Higgsfield. Upload one photo and swap yourself into one of our effects or into a video you upload.
landing.faq.free.question: Can I try it for free?
landing.faq.free.answer: Registration and examples are free; all video generation requires payment first. Packs start at $9.90 with no subscription, and technical failures restore the deducted balance.

frog.meta.title: Crazy Frog AI Video Generator | Genjutsu AI
frog.meta.description: Make a Crazy Frog AI chase video from one photo. Pick a built-in chase theme or upload your own clip, then ride an invisible motorcycle.
frog.hero.title: Crazy Frog AI
frog.hero.description: Upload your photo, choose a chase theme and become the rider on an invisible motorcycle. The selected scene supplies the action, camera movement and pursuer.
frog.hero.note: One photo. Pick a theme. No prompt writing.
frog.studio.title: Take the rider’s place.
frog.studio.description: Choose a scene or upload your own video, add one clear photo and click Generate. A built-in theme supplies the reference video automatically.
frog.about.title: What is Crazy Frog AI?
frog.about.body: Crazy Frog AI is a short-video format inspired by the imaginary motorcycle pose associated with Crazy Frog. A person crouches low, reaches forward as though holding handlebars and races along a road with nothing underneath them. A pursuer follows, turning an impossible ride into a playful chase. The contrast between a recognizable person and the invisible vehicle is the joke.
frog.about.more: Your photo defines the rider’s appearance, while the selected built-in theme supplies the action. This editor replaces the main rider while preserving the scene, camera movement and pursuer.
frog.steps.title: Your photo. Your turn to escape.
frog.steps.intro: Your photo defines the rider. Choose the world you want to escape through and let the built-in scene supply the action.
frog.steps.one.title: Choose your chase theme
frog.steps.one.body: Choose from the overpass, neon city, chocolate factory, pixel world, circuit board or Halloween chase, and preview the prepared 10-second scene before generating. Prefer your own footage? Upload a clip of a crouching rider instead.
frog.steps.two.title: Add your rider photo
frog.steps.two.body: Choose one person with a sharp, visible face and even lighting. Include shoulders and some of the outfit rather than using a very tight face crop. Avoid group photos, sunglasses and heavy beauty filters. Use your own photo or a person who has agreed to this edit.
frog.steps.three.title: Generate and review
frog.steps.three.body: Check the reference framing and displayed cost before starting. Sign in and use your existing balance, or choose a credit pack when prompted. When the video finishes, inspect the face, hands and chase sequence, then download it. Your account’s video history provides another place to find the result.
frog.check.title: Keep the chase recognizable.
frog.check.intro: A good Crazy Frog AI video depends on the source action as much as the photo. Check these details before spending a generation.
frog.check.one.title: An invisible ride
frog.check.one.body: The source should clearly show the low riding pose without a motorcycle under the main character. The editing direction asks the model to preserve that illusion. AI can still invent a wheel, seat or handlebar, so inspect the result instead of assuming every frame will be exact.
frog.check.two.title: Room for the pursuer
frog.check.two.body: Match the reference’s framing. A horizontal chase may need its full width to show both people, and cropping it vertically can remove the pursuer. Choose a source composed for your intended format. A vertical export and a native vertical scene are different things.
frog.check.three.title: Sound you expect
frog.check.three.body: Audio depends on the source clip and configured generation provider. This page does not supply a licensed Axel F recording. Check what your export contains and add suitable music in your publishing app when you have permission to use it. The sample player’s mute switch controls playback only.
frog.faq.title: Before you hit the road.
frog.faq.one.a: Reading this page and viewing the illustration are free. Making a personalized video uses paid generation credits. The editor shows pricing information before you start. There is no free personalized video preview on this page, and uploading a photo alone does not create a finished chase.
frog.faq.two.q: Do I need to upload a reference video?
frog.faq.two.a: No, it is optional. Choose one of the six built-in themes and the editor prepares the reference video automatically. If you have your own chase clip, upload it with the Upload video card instead. Either way, one clear photo replaces the main rider.
frog.faq.three.q: Can I replace the person chasing me too?
frog.faq.three.a: This version replaces the main rider only; the pursuer stays as filmed. Separate casting needs more identity testing, especially during close-ups. A second face will not automatically replace the pursuer.
frog.faq.four.q: Will the result match every frame?
frog.faq.four.a: The workflow aims to preserve the source action while replacing the rider, but AI edits can change faces, clothing, hands and small objects between frames. Fast flips and occlusion are especially demanding. Use the result viewer to check the entire clip before sharing it.
frog.faq.five.a: Follow the task status and error message in the editor. A technical failure and a completed video with an unwanted visual detail are different outcomes. Existing account and credit rules apply; this page does not promise a free retry for every aesthetic issue. Keep the task in your history if you need support.
frog.faq.six.q: Is this an official Crazy Frog product?
frog.faq.six.a: No. This independent editing page is not affiliated with or endorsed by Crazy Frog or its rights holders. Use media you have permission to edit. Footage, music and photos have permissions separate from this tool.
frog.cta.title: Bring the face. Keep the chase.
frog.cta.body: Choose your theme and add your photo. Your chase starts in the editor.

ozil.eyebrow: The TikTok goal trend, starring you
ozil.hero.title: Ozil AI
ozil.hero.description: Upload one photo and take the scorer’s place in the Ozil goal that is all over TikTok. The keeper, the two sliding defenders and the stadium stay as filmed; the player who finishes the move becomes you.
ozil.strip.three: Keeper and defenders stay in the shot
ozil.studio.title: Step into the Ozil goal.
ozil.studio.description: Pick one of the three goal takes, add a clear photo of one person and click Generate. You can also upload your own football clip of three to ten seconds.
ozil.price: Starter pack: {price}. Check the editor for your balance and generation cost.
ozil.examples.title: Three takes of the same goal.
ozil.examples.description: Every take follows the same move with a different scorer. Pick the outfit closest to your photo for the most natural result.
ozil.examples.note: These previews are the reference takes the editor starts from, not personalized results.
ozil.about.title: What is Ozil AI?
ozil.about.line: One touch over the keeper. One pause. One empty net.
ozil.about.body: Ozil AI is the name TikTok gave to a wave of AI edits built on one of Mesut Özil’s most replayed goals. On 1 November 2016, Arsenal came from two goals down to win 3–2 at Ludogorets in the Champions League group stage. Özil’s late winner began with a soft chip over the onrushing goalkeeper. Instead of shooting straight away, he waited with the ball at his feet, let two defenders slide past him and rolled it calmly into the empty net.
ozil.about.more: In October 2026, edits that put someone else in Özil’s place started spreading on TikTok, and “ozil ai” became the search people used to make their own. The joke works because the move is so relaxed: the person in the clip looks completely unbothered while two professionals throw themselves at the ball. This page lets you make that edit from a single photo, with your whole figure redrawn rather than a face pasted on top.
ozil.steps.title: From one photo to the winner.
ozil.steps.intro: Your photo defines the scorer. The goal take supplies the run, the chip, the pause and the finish.
ozil.steps.one.title: Choose a goal take
ozil.steps.one.body: Pick the red hoodie, five-a-side or office shirt take. All three show the same move. A take whose outfit and build are close to your photo usually needs less change, so the result tends to look more natural.
ozil.steps.two.title: Add your scorer photo
ozil.steps.two.body: Use one person facing the camera, with even light and nothing covering the face. A waist-up or full-length photo works better than a tight selfie, because the edit has to fill a whole running body. Group shots, heavy filters and sunglasses make results less predictable.
ozil.steps.three.title: Generate and post
ozil.steps.three.body: Check the displayed cost, sign in and click Generate. A 10-second take usually finishes in a few minutes. You get a vertical 9:16 MP4 to download and post on TikTok, Reels or Shorts, with the trend sound added in the app.
ozil.check.title: Make the goal look real.
ozil.check.intro: An Ozil AI edit convinces people when the move reads clearly. Check these details before you spend credits.
ozil.check.one.title: A full-body scorer
ozil.check.one.body: The scorer is visible from head to boots and turns several times. A photo that shows your shoulders and outfit helps the edit keep your build consistent from the chip to the finish.
ozil.check.two.title: Leave the defenders alone
ozil.check.two.body: Only the scorer changes. The keeper’s dive and both slide tackles stay as filmed, which is exactly what makes the pause look so cool. Do not expect extra players or a new celebration.
ozil.check.three.title: Add the sound when posting
ozil.check.three.body: The goal takes are silent. Add the trending audio inside TikTok or Instagram when you post, so the platform links your video to the trend and handles the music licence.
ozil.compare.title: Templates, prompts or a full recast?
ozil.compare.intro: There are three common ways to make the Ozil goal video, and they solve different problems.
ozil.compare.template.title: Face-swap templates
ozil.compare.template.body: Fast and cheap, but they paste a face over the original player. Hair, skin tone and body stay the same, so the clip can look like a sticker once the player turns away from the camera.
ozil.compare.prompt.title: Text-to-video prompts
ozil.compare.prompt.body: Prompt tools generate a brand-new goal from a description. You get an original stadium and players, but the famous chip, pause and finish rarely come out the way viewers recognise them.
ozil.compare.recast.title: Reference recast (this page)
ozil.compare.recast.body: The take keeps the real movement and camera, and the whole scorer, including face, hair and build, is redrawn from your photo. It uses credits and takes a few minutes, but it is the closest match to the clips in the trend.
ozil.faq.title: Before kick-off.
ozil.faq.one.a: Reading this page and playing the previews is free. Making a personalized video uses paid generation credits, and the editor shows the cost before you start. There is no free personalized preview.
ozil.faq.two.q: Can I use a friend’s photo or my pet?
ozil.faq.two.a: Only use photos of people who have agreed to appear in your video. Pets and drawn characters can work, but because the take shows a running person, the result is less predictable than with a human photo.
ozil.faq.three.a: Most 10-second takes finish within a few minutes. You can keep the page open or come back later; finished videos are saved under My Work in your account.
ozil.faq.four.q: Can I post it on TikTok?
ozil.faq.four.a: Yes. Download the MP4 and post it like any other video. Add the trend sound in the app and label the clip as AI-generated where the platform asks you to.
ozil.faq.five.a: If the task fails for a technical reason, its credits are returned to your balance automatically. A finished video with a detail you do not like is a different outcome and is not refunded, so check the photo tips before generating.
ozil.faq.six.q: Is this connected to Mesut Özil or Arsenal?
ozil.faq.six.a: No. Genjutsu AI is an independent editing tool and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mesut Özil, Arsenal, Ludogorets, UEFA or any broadcaster. “Ozil AI” is simply the name of the trend.
ozil.cta.title: Your turn to roll it in.
ozil.cta.body: Pick a take, add your photo and score the goal everyone is copying.

flycar.meta.description: Make a Flying Car AI video from one photo of your car. It climbs a curved ramp, flips upside down, launches into the air and lands in smoke. No prompt needed.
flycar.eyebrow: The Roadster ramp trend, with your car
flycar.hero.title: Flying Car AI
flycar.hero.generator: your car, up the ramp and into the air
flycar.hero.description: Upload one photo of your car, van or truck. Flying Car AI puts it on a towering curved ramp, drives it upside down, launches it off the top and lands it in a cloud of smoke. A 10-second stunt video, no prompt to write.

flycar.strip.three: Same body, paint and wheels in every shot

flycar.price: Starter pack: {price}. Check the editor for your balance and generation cost.
flycar.generator.title: Make your car fly
flycar.generator.photo_hint: Whole vehicle in frame, side or three-quarter view
flycar.generator.retry: Stunt could not load. Click to retry.
flycar.examples.title: The stunt, four ways
flycar.examples.description: Every clip runs the same route: up the curved ramp, upside down at the top, a flip through the air and a landing in smoke. Hover or tap to play.
flycar.examples.note: Sample stunts for illustration. This generator is tuned for cars, vans, pickups and trucks; results can vary.
flycar.about.title: From a ramp in Texas to your feed
flycar.about.line: The joke is simple: the car that flies is the one you actually drive.
flycar.about.body: On 15 October 2026, Tesla unveiled its new Roadster at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas. A driverless prototype climbed a curved ramp until it was hanging upside down, fired cold-gas thrusters, flipped through the air and landed. A second run cleared a row of parked cars. It was a short, controlled hop rather than real flight, but the footage spread everywhere within hours.
flycar.about.more: Within a day, people were remaking it with AI. Instead of a six-figure sports car, the vehicle on the ramp became a family minivan, a delivery van, a rusty hatchback or a pickup with a ladder rack. Those Flying Car AI clips took over TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, usually captioned with something like "Waiting for my Roadster like…".
flycar.about.third: This page makes that stunt with your own vehicle. You upload one photo; the editor keeps the ramp, the camera angles, the flip and the smoke from a built-in reference and replaces only the vehicle. Genjutsu AI is an independent tool and is not affiliated with Tesla or any car maker.
flycar.steps.title: How to make a Flying Car AI video
flycar.steps.intro: Three steps, about a minute of your time. The render itself takes a few minutes.
flycar.steps.one.title: Upload your car
flycar.steps.one.body: Pick a sharp daylight photo with the whole vehicle in frame. Side or three-quarter views work best, because the stunt shows the car from the back, the top and the front.
flycar.steps.two.title: Generate the stunt
flycar.steps.two.body: Confirm you can use the photo and press generate. The editor swaps your car into the reference stunt and keeps every camera move, the flip and the landing.
flycar.steps.three.title: Download and post
flycar.steps.three.body: Watch the result, download the MP4 and add a trending sound in TikTok, Reels or your editor. Your video stays in My work if you want it again later.
flycar.check.title: Photo tips for a clean flight
flycar.check.intro: The photo decides how convincing the result looks. These three checks fix most problems before you spend credits.
flycar.check.one.title: The whole vehicle, nothing cropped
flycar.check.one.body: Bumpers, roof and all visible wheels should be inside the frame. A cropped nose or roof leaves the AI guessing, and guesses show up during the flip.
flycar.check.two.title: One vehicle, plain background
flycar.check.two.body: Avoid busy car parks and overlapping cars. If other vehicles are in the shot, crop them out so the editor knows exactly which one to put on the ramp.
flycar.check.three.title: Even light, no heavy glare
flycar.check.three.body: Overcast daylight or open shade keeps paint colour and badges readable. Night shots and strong reflections make the body shape harder to hold.
flycar.ideas.title: Flying car video ideas that land
flycar.ideas.intro: The stunt is the same for everyone, so the caption and the car do the work.
flycar.ideas.one.title: Waiting for my Roadster
flycar.ideas.one.body: Use your oldest, most ordinary car and caption it as if it is the real thing. The bigger the gap, the better it plays.
flycar.ideas.two.title: The work van takes off
flycar.ideas.two.body: Plumbers, florists and food trucks: a branded van flipping off the ramp is an ad people actually share.
flycar.ideas.three.title: First car, first flight
flycar.ideas.three.body: Just passed your test or bought your first car? Make its first trip a ramp launch and post it with the keys.
flycar.ideas.four.title: Dream build reveal
flycar.ideas.four.body: Got a render or a photo of the build you are saving for? Launch it now and pin the clip until it is real.
flycar.faq.title: Flying Car AI questions
flycar.faq.one.q: What is the Flying Car AI trend?
flycar.faq.one.a: It is a wave of short AI videos that started after the Tesla Roadster demo on 15 October 2026, where the car climbed a curved ramp, flipped through the air and landed. Creators remake the stunt with their own everyday cars.
flycar.faq.two.q: What kind of photo should I upload?
flycar.faq.two.a: One clear photo of a single vehicle with the whole body and wheels in frame, ideally a side or three-quarter view in daylight. Cars, SUVs, vans, pickups and trucks all work.
flycar.faq.three.q: How long is the video and what size is it?
flycar.faq.three.a: The stunt runs for 10 seconds in widescreen 16:9. It covers the climb, the upside-down section, the launch and flip, and the smoke landing.
flycar.faq.four.q: Do I need to write a prompt?
flycar.faq.four.a: No. The stunt, the camera moves and the scene are built in. You only provide the photo of your vehicle.
flycar.faq.five.q: Is this an official Tesla product?
flycar.faq.five.a: No. Genjutsu AI is independent and not affiliated with or endorsed by Tesla. The video is an AI edit for entertainment and does not show a real vehicle flying.
flycar.faq.six.q: Can I post the video on TikTok and Instagram?
flycar.faq.six.a: Yes, once you download it. Platforms ask you to label AI-generated content, so turn on the AI label when you post. Only use photos of vehicles you have the right to use.
flycar.cta.title: Your car has never left the ground. Yet.
flycar.cta.body: One photo is all it takes to send it up the ramp, flip it over and land it in smoke.
